note: Ferme is the noun 'farm' and adjective 'firm'; the same spelling is also the verb form 'closes/shuts' from fermer. The specialized roof-truss sense should not obscure those basics.
proposed_english: farm; firm; closes/shuts (form of fermer); roof truss (specialized)

note: Complètement is an adverb meaning completely/entirely/fully. The noun label is dictionary noise for this learner entry.
Doute is the noun 'doubt', but it is also a common finite/imperative form of douter ('doubts; doubt!').
proposed_english: doubt; doubts; doubt! (forms of douter, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Approcher means approach/bring closer; in reflexive use s'approcher means come near/approach. 'Bring close together' alone is too narrow.
proposed_english: to approach; to bring closer; to come near/approach (s'approcher)

note: The current entry gives only the anatomical vulgar noun. In modern colloquial French, con is very commonly the adjective/noun insult 'stupid; idiot/jerk/asshole'. Register must be explicit.
proposed_english: stupid; dumb; idiot; jerk/asshole; cunt (vulgar, context-dependent)

note: The entry lists noun/verb POS but gives only noun senses. Lancer as a verb means throw, launch, start/set off; as a noun it can mean throw/pitch/shot.
proposed_english: to throw; to launch; to start/set off; throw; pitch; shot

note: Fier is the adjective proud, while se fier à means trust/rely on and the rare transitive fier can entrust. The verb POS has no matching meaning in the current entry.
proposed_english: proud; to trust/rely on (se fier à); to entrust (rare/formal)

note: Bordel is vulgar/informal. It means brothel and colloquially a mess/chaos or an exclamation like damn/fuck; the register must be labeled.
For learner use autour is the adverb 'around' and occurs in autour de = around/about. The noun label reflects an unrelated rare homograph and adds noise.
Règle means rule/regulation and also the common physical noun ruler; the same form is also a finite verb form of régler. 'Ruler' is missing.
proposed_english: rule; regulation; ruler; regulates/adjusts (form of régler, context-dependent)

note: Journal means newspaper/journal/diary/log and can mean a news bulletin. 'Newsbreak' is not the best learner gloss, and diary/journal is missing.
proposed_english: newspaper; journal; diary; log; news bulletin

note: Dégager centrally means clear/free/release and give off/emit. 'Get out of here' is the imperative/slang use dégage!, not the general infinitive meaning.
proposed_english: to clear; to free; to release; to give off/emit; get out! (dégage!, informal)

note: Ennemi can be the noun enemy and the adjective enemy/hostile; adjective POS is listed but the adjective meaning is missing.
Bare retirer means remove/withdraw/take out/take off. 'Retire/withdraw oneself' is commonly se retirer; the entry should distinguish the reflexive use.
proposed_english: to remove; to withdraw; to take out; to take off; to retire/withdraw oneself (se retirer)
